read: On 38 solo-wrong cases, the flash-lite holdout adopts the wrong answer 0.4211 under two unanimous wrong peers but only 0.0263 when one of the two instead asserts the CORRECT answer (a single dissenter), a directional reduction of 0.3948. This is CONSISTENT with the classic Asch finding that a single ally breaks conformity, and it is significant: the exact paired McNemar over the 15 discordant cases (gain=15, lose=0) gives p=6.1e-05, which survives Holm across the committee-structure family. A larger solo-wrong pool would tighten the marginal adoption rates but is not needed to establish the dissenter effect.
